task.title: Derive indexed fixed-interval occurrence instants
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/855 by calculating caller-owned zero-based fixed-interval occurrence instants in constant time without persisting recurrence.
acceptance_criteria: Return the anchor for offset zero, preserve one-step equivalence for offset one, and derive ordinary offsets with checked multiplication and addition.
Accept every exactly representable result including u64::MAX and preserve the anchor, interval, and offset on either overflow stage.
Keep the existing one-step API compatible and document the absence of persistence, occurrence identity, catch-up, clock, dispatch, and execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused kernel test failed to compile with six E0599 diagnostics because ScheduleInstant::checked_advance_by did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for offsets zero and one, ordinary indexed advancement, exact u64::MAX, multiplication overflow, addition overflow, and typed operand accessors.

attempts.diagnostic: Repeated one-step advancement would be proportional to the occurrence offset, while unchecked multiplication could wrap before checked addition observed the elapsed duration.
attempts.patch: Added checked_advance_by and ScheduleOccurrenceError using checked multiplication and addition, preserved the one-step API, and recorded zero-based semantics and authority exclusions in ADR-0036 and scheduler documentation.

attempts.summary: Completed substantive exact-head review after a false-green cooldown.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit initially reported Review limit reached even though its status context was green, so that run could not satisfy the review gate.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled, waited past the stated cooldown, deliberately resumed one review, and merged only after CodeRabbit reviewed all five changed files with no actionable comments and zero unresolved threads.

outcome.summary: Callers can derive exact zero-based fixed-interval occurrence instants in constant time with typed evidence for multiplication or addition overflow.

lessons: Zero-based occurrence arithmetic keeps the immutable anchor at offset zero and makes anchor plus interval times offset explicit.
Check multiplication before addition so large offsets cannot wrap into apparently valid elapsed durations.
An arithmetic offset is caller-owned input, not durable occurrence identity, execution count, authorization, or catch-up policy.
A false-green rate-limited review must be deliberately resumed after cooldown and completed on the exact head before merge.
